old:783|A|A3|crest|What belongs in penetration-test rules of engagement?|Scope, permitted methods, constraints, and escalation|Only the final severity rankings|Only the scanner's default settings|Only the customer's public address range|RoE defines the operating agreement, including testing windows and contacts. A target inventory is only one component.|A scope list alone is not a complete operating agreement.

old:784|A|A1|crest|What primarily distinguishes white-box from black-box assessment?|The internal information provided to the tester|Whether the test is lawful|Whether all tests are automated|Whether the application uses TLS|White-box testing provides internal information such as source and configuration. Either format can be authorized and can use manual and automated work.|Information access and testing technique are different dimensions.

old:785|A|A1|crest|What is the principal client benefit of a penetration test?|Evidence about exploitable weaknesses and improvement priorities|A guarantee that no vulnerability remains|Automatic certification of legal compliance|A replacement for ongoing patch management|A bounded assessment can expose and contextualize weaknesses. It cannot exhaust every future attack or replace continuing controls.|A useful assessment does not imply a security guarantee.

old:786|A|A2|cma|Which UK statute principally addresses unauthorized access to computer material?|Computer Misuse Act 1990|Human Rights Act 1998|Data Protection Act 2018|Freedom of Information Act 2000|The CMA addresses specified computer misuse offenses. Privacy and personal-data obligations arise through other legal frameworks as well.|Choose the law matching the conduct, not just any security-related law.

old:789|A|A2|cma|Which CMA section concerns unauthorized acts intended, or reckless as to, impairing computer operation?|Section 3|Section 1|Section 2|Section 3A|Section 3 addresses impairment-related acts. Sections 1 and 2 address unauthorized access and further-offense intent; section 3A concerns articles for specified offenses.|Access, impairment, and tool-related offenses differ.

old:790|A|A3|crest|What is the purpose of estimating testing resources during scoping?|Align effort with assets, objectives, and available time|Set severity before evidence is collected|Guarantee every host will be compromised|Make vulnerability validation unnecessary|Resource planning helps set a credible coverage and timescale. It does not predefine technical outcomes.|Effort estimates describe work, not guaranteed findings.

old:792|A|A4|crest|What is residual risk?|Risk remaining after controls are applied|Risk assessed before controls exist|Risk transferred without any remaining consequence|Risk eliminated by the report's publication|Controls reduce or modify risk; residual risk remains for further treatment or acceptance.|Risk treatment does not necessarily eliminate risk.

old:793|A|A4|crest|Which risk can testing itself introduce?|Service disruption or unintended data exposure|Only risks already present before testing|Only inaccurate scanner branding|Only changes in the client's marketing budget|Testing actions can affect availability, confidentiality, and integrity. Plan limits, escalation, evidence handling, and recovery.|The assessment process has its own operational risks.

old:796|A|A5|crest|Who is the executive summary primarily written to inform?|Decision-makers about business risk and priorities|Only exploit developers reproducing shellcode|Only network tools parsing machine-readable output|Only the tester's personal revision notes|An executive summary connects major findings to business consequences and decisions. Reproduction detail belongs in supporting technical findings.|A report needs different levels of detail for different readers.

old:797|A|A5|crest|Why retain structured notes during a test?|Support accurate reporting and reproducible findings|Replace evidence with memory of tool output|Increase the number of severity labels|Prove every scanner warning is exploitable|Record actions, identity, time, observations, and interpretation as work proceeds. This supports verification and avoids retrospective invention.|A remembered conclusion is weaker than retained causal evidence.

old:801|A|A1|crest|What is a useful purpose of the final debrief?|Explain findings, limitations, and remediation priorities|Expand scope after all testing is complete|Replace the written report with oral claims|Promise the environment is permanently secure|A debrief lets stakeholders question conclusions and understand next actions. It complements the durable report.|Communication and evidence should support one another.

old:955|A|A1|crest|How does penetration testing generally differ from a vulnerability assessment?|It validates selected attack paths and consequences|It never uses automated discovery|It must compromise every listed asset|It is limited to checking version banners|Assessments identify candidate weaknesses; penetration tests investigate practical exploitation within scope. Both can use automation and have coverage limits.|The distinction is not simply manual versus automated work.

old:170|C|C2|dnsbase|Which is a conventional DNS resource-record type?|HINFO|NWS|MAILHOST|DOMAINOWNER|HINFO describes host hardware and operating-system information. The other names are not the conventional record types offered here.|DNS terminology must match actual record types.

old:220|C|C2|dnsbase|Which query targets a BIND version-disclosure TXT record in the CHAOS class?|nslookup -q=txt -class=CHAOS version.bind SERVER|nslookup -q=mx version.bind SERVER|nslookup -q=ptr -class=IN version.bind SERVER|nslookup -q=soa example.test SERVER|This requests version.bind in the CHAOS class. The server may suppress or customize its reply; do not treat a string as verified patch status.|Class, type, and owner name all affect the query.

old:422|C|C2|dnsbase|In SOA 'ns.example.test. hostmaster.example.test. 2026101401 3600 600 86400 300', which value is the serial?|2026101401|3600|86400|300|The first numeric SOA field after server and mailbox is the serial. The following values are refresh, retry, expire, and minimum.|Read field position rather than guessing from a large number.

old:428|C|C2|dnsbase|What is a DNS zone?|An administratively served portion of the DNS namespace|Every name beneath a domain regardless of delegation|A TCP connection to an authoritative server|A resolver's list of cached client queries|Delegation can split a domain subtree into separately administered zones. A zone and a domain are related, but not interchangeable.|Subdomains can lie in different zones.

old:526|C|C1|crest|Which activity is passive relative to the target's systems?|Reading a third-party registry's published record|Requesting the target's robots.txt directly|Attempting an AXFR against the target nameserver|Crawling every page on the target server|Third-party published data avoids direct contact with the target service. That does not guarantee secrecy from every observer.|Passive describes the collection relationship, not invisibility.

old:528|C|C3|crest|What is a benefit of making an authorized local copy of public site content?|Repeatable offline review of the captured material|A guarantee that every authenticated route was captured|Automatic access to the backend database|A guarantee that the content remains current|A snapshot supports review and comparison but has capture-time and coverage limits. Authenticated and dynamic behavior may require separate collection.|A mirror is a snapshot, not a complete application model.

old:674|C|C5|nntp|What is NNTP used for?|Transferring and accessing network news articles|Issuing DNS authoritative responses|Transferring SSH host keys|Resolving Ethernet neighbor addresses|NNTP supports article transfer and access to newsgroups. Public archives can expose historical technical information about organizations.|News infrastructure can be an information source without being a test target.

old:716|C|C1|crest|Which transport and port conventionally serve WHOIS?|TCP/43|UDP/43|TCP/53|UDP/53|Traditional WHOIS uses TCP/43. Modern registration lookup may instead use HTTPS-based RDAP.|Identify the lookup protocol rather than assuming all registry access is WHOIS.

old:823|C|C2|dnsbase|Which DNS record identifies a domain's mail exchangers?|MX|PTR|HINFO|SOA|MX names mail exchangers with preference values. PTR maps addresses back to names, while SOA describes zone administration.|Mail routing is not reverse name resolution.

old:825|C|C2|dnsbase|What information is conventionally represented by an HINFO record?|CPU and operating-system descriptions|Mail-server priority and hostname|Zone refresh and retry intervals|A hostname's IPv6 address|HINFO can describe platform details. Records may be absent, stale, or intentionally uninformative.|A record's defined purpose does not guarantee an accurate disclosure.

old:826|C|C1|crest|Which information can domain registration data potentially expose?|Registrar, lifecycle dates, and name-server associations|A complete list of application users|Every database password on the website|The exact live firewall rules|Registration data is useful context; privacy and registry policy limit available fields. It is not a technical inventory of the service.|Public registration is evidence of registration, not all infrastructure.

old:938|C|C2|dnsbase|Which resource-record type identifies authoritative name servers for a zone?|NS|MX|TXT|PTR|NS records identify nameservers. Address records and sometimes glue are needed to reach them, depending on delegation context.|A nameserver name is not itself an IP address.

old:186|I|I3|sqli|Which function conventionally introduces a MySQL query delay?|SLEEP(5)|pg_sleep(5)|DBMS_SESSION.SLEEP(5)|WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:05'|These constructs belong to different engines. MySQL supports SLEEP; injection context still determines how to form a valid test.|Identify the backend before selecting a dialect-specific probe.

old:286|I|I2|xss|Why can an automated reflected-XSS check miss stored XSS?|Submission and later rendering may occur on different routes or roles|Stored payloads cannot contain JavaScript|Stored XSS requires all victims to disable TLS|A database always encrypts stored scripts|Stored content may execute in another workflow or privileged view. Testing must connect the write and render paths.|A single request/response is not every application's execution path.

old:291|I|I3|sqli|What is the intended role of an injected OR condition such as OR 1=1?|Change a query's predicate logic|Change the web server's TCP port|Create a JavaScript browser event handler|Authenticate a TLS certificate|A tautology may alter SQL filtering or authentication logic if it enters query syntax. Reflection of the string alone does not prove injection.|Payload purpose and successful execution are different claims.

old:530|I|I3|sqli|A UNION query requests banner from Oracle's v$version. What is the tester seeking?|Database version information|The operating-system password file|The browser's session storage|A wireless network's SSID|v$version exposes Oracle version-related information when accessible. UNION shape and account privileges still constrain the attempt.|A known metadata target does not guarantee access.

old:829|I|I3|sqli|Why might a tester begin with a single quote in a suspected string parameter?|Probe whether input affects SQL syntax handling|Prove every table can be dropped|Determine a cookie's cryptographic entropy|Prove the backend is PostgreSQL|A quote can produce a useful parsing signal, but controlled follow-up is required and some inputs are safely handled.|A first probe is a lead, not a complete finding.

old:830|I|I3|sqli|What makes an SQL injection technique 'blind'?|Data is inferred through indirect observable effects|The attacker cannot see any HTTP response|The request is always encrypted with TLS|The database has no user accounts|Boolean, timing, and other effects can reveal information without directly returning selected rows.|Blind does not mean there are no observations.

old:831|I|I3|sqli|What does UNION-based SQL injection generally attempt?|Combine an injected SELECT result with the original result|Replace every application query with a stored procedure|Encrypt the original table with a session key|Reconfigure the database listener's network port|UNION combines result sets with compatible column counts and types. Application output and privileges determine what is exposed.|Syntax compatibility is only one prerequisite.

old:832|I|I1|http|What does a link-following spider primarily discover?|Reachable links and application navigation structure|Every unlinked file on disk|Every server-side authorization rule|The complete database schema|Crawling follows discoverable navigation within its state and access. Forced browsing and source inspection complement it.|Linked-content discovery is not exhaustive route discovery.

old:834|I|I4|http|What does an intercepting web proxy let a tester inspect and alter?|HTTP requests and responses in the proxied flow|Every process's memory on the server|Every client's wireless encryption key|The database's internal permissions automatically|A proxy gives control over observed application traffic. Use it to test client-controlled parameters and compare server behavior.|Traffic control is not automatic control over the backend.

old:541|I|I4|http|A requested path contains ..%255c..%255c. What transformation is the tester probing?|Multiple decoding into parent-directory separators|RSA public-key encryption of a session cookie|DNS compression of a mail-server hostname|TCP reassembly of a fragmented TLS record|%25 decodes to a percent sign; a subsequent pass can decode %5c to backslash. Whether traversal succeeds depends on the application and filesystem.|Track each decoding pass and the platform's separators.

old:512|I|I1|crest|Why should old IIS extension paths matter during an assessment of a legacy server?|An exposed extension may add its own vulnerable request handler|Every extension grants anonymous SYSTEM access|Extensions replace all application authorization checks|IIS extensions can only process encrypted inputs|Legacy handlers have their own code and configuration. Confirm exact applicability rather than inferring compromise from a path.|An installed component and an exploitable instance are different facts.

old:642|I|I4|command|Untrusted input is interpreted as shell syntax rather than one data argument. Which issue is most specific?|OS command injection|SQL injection|Cross-site request forgery|Directory-listing disclosure|The interpreter receiving the input determines the injection class. Shell escaping or avoiding a shell matters; SQL parameters address a different sink.|Name the interpreter that crosses the data/code boundary.

old:274|J|J3|crest|Which TCP port conventionally serves a MySQL server?|3306|5432|1433|1521|3306 is the conventional MySQL port; PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Oracle commonly use the other listed ports. Configuration can change them.|A default port is a clue, not authenticated service identification.

old:282|J|J3|crest|Within an authenticated MySQL SQL session, which query returns server version information?|SELECT VERSION();|SELECT SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion');|SELECT * FROM v$version;|SHOW SERVER BUILD;|SELECT VERSION() is conventional MySQL syntax. A client executable's --version output may describe the client instead of the connected server.|Client and server versions need not match.

old:32|J|J2|oracle|DBSNMP appears in an Oracle account inventory. What function is that account associated with?|Database monitoring and management support|The operating-system root account|Every application's end-user session|The network's DNS signing key|DBSNMP is a recognizable Oracle account to review for status and privileges. Do not assume its password from its name or an old installation default.|Account purpose is not a credential guarantee.

old:174|J|J2|oracle|Which TCP port is conventionally associated with the Oracle TNS listener?|1521|1433|3306|5432|1521 is conventional; deployed listeners may use other ports. A listener brokers connections to configured database services.|The listener port does not establish database login privileges.

old:177|J|J2|oracle|An authenticated Oracle query reads V$VERSION. What does it primarily provide?|Database version component information|Every schema's plaintext passwords|The host's active Ethernet neighbors|A writable list of firewall rules|Version metadata supports applicability checks. Patch evidence can require further component and inventory information.|A version banner is not a complete security patch assessment.

old:542|J|J1|sql|Which SQL Server feature can run operating-system commands when enabled and permitted?|xp_cmdshell|sp_who|sp_helptext|SELECT DB_NAME()|xp_cmdshell crosses into OS command execution under a configured account. The other choices provide database/session information.|Command execution depends on enablement, caller rights, and execution identity.

old:548|J|J2|oracle|Why are historical Oracle default credentials worth recognizing during legacy assessments?|They suggest bounded, version-aware checks for unchanged installations|They prove all modern installations share the same password|They establish remote SYSDBA access on every listener|They remove the need to verify account lockout behavior|Historical knowledge helps form hypotheses. Installer behavior, account state, version, and current credentials still need validation.|Historical defaults are not universal current facts.

old:549|J|J2|oracle|Which pair is conventionally recognized as a historical Oracle demonstration account?|SCOTT / TIGER|sa / guest|root / toor|postgres / postgres|SCOTT/TIGER is associated with sample schemas in older material. Availability and authentication depend on installation and configuration.|A sample account is not necessarily present or enabled.

old:737|J|J1|sql|What is SQL Server Browser's conventional network role?|Map instance discovery requests to instance connection details|Execute arbitrary commands as every database login|Store all Windows domain password hashes|Encrypt HTTP responses from the application|Browser commonly uses UDP/1434 for instance discovery. A named instance can listen on a dynamically selected TCP port.|Discovery service and database data connection are different flows.

old:892|J|J1|sql|What does TCP/1433 conventionally identify in SQL Server deployments?|The default instance's database connection endpoint|The Browser service's UDP discovery endpoint|Every named instance's mandatory fixed endpoint|The Windows domain controller's LDAP endpoint|A default instance commonly uses TCP/1433; named-instance and custom-port configurations differ.|Specify the instance and transport when describing default ports.

old:897|J|J1|sqlroles|What is the usual role associated with SQL Server's built-in sa login?|Server-level system administration|Only one database's read-only reporting|An operating-system account on every client|Only the Browser service's anonymous discovery|The sa login is a powerful database-engine principal. It can be disabled or renamed and is not itself a Windows user.|Database privilege and operating-system identity must be assessed separately.

old:898|J|J1|sqlroles|What does SELECT @@VERSION conventionally retrieve in SQL Server?|Server build and version information|The current application's source code|A Kerberos service ticket|The caller's plaintext Windows password|Version output supports identification but must be combined with current patch/applicability evidence.|Fingerprinting is not a demonstration of exploitability.

old:803|H|H4|authn|How can different messages for unknown user and wrong password weaken login security?|They reveal account-existence signals|They increase the password's entropy|They prove the session cookie is predictable|They disable the need for MFA|An attacker may distinguish existing accounts. Messages, timing, and other observable differences all merit review.|A generic message alone may not remove every enumeration signal.

old:804|H|H4|authn|Which pair combines two different authentication factor categories?|Hardware token and memorized PIN|Password and security-question answer|Fingerprint and iris scan|Username and account number|Possession plus knowledge is two categories. Two knowledge checks or two biometrics are not two different factor categories.|More prompts are not necessarily more factors.

old:806|H|H6|authz|What does an allowlist validation strategy do?|Permit input matching explicitly allowed forms|Reject only substrings already seen in attacks|Treat all client-generated data as trusted|Guarantee correct authorization for every request|An allowlist defines acceptable syntax or values. It complements, rather than replaces, context-aware output handling and permission checks.|Validation and authorization solve different problems.

old:807|H|H6|authz|Why must important input constraints be enforced on the server?|A client can submit requests without the normal browser validation|The browser always converts all input to SQL|TLS removes every client-side validation rule|Only a proxy can ever change a hidden field|Custom requests can bypass normal client code. Enforce business and syntax constraints where the trusted action happens.|Client convenience checks are not the authoritative boundary.

old:808|H|H8|err|Which disclosure is a detailed application stack trace likely to contain?|Internal code paths and component details|Every user's current password|The TLS client's private signing key|The complete router forwarding table|Paths, class names, versions, and query information can assist later testing. Actual disclosure depends on the trace.|An error message is useful evidence without proving every possible impact.

old:810|H|H10|sqli|Which outcome can SQL injection directly enable when the DB account can read sensitive tables?|Unauthorized retrieval of those tables' data|Automatic elevation to kernel privileges|Automatic bypass of every MFA deployment|Mandatory decryption of all external TLS sessions|Query manipulation can expose data reachable by the connection's rights. Other outcomes require additional permissions and mechanisms.|Tie claimed impact to the actual database authority.

old:811|H|H10|ldap|Which structure is directly manipulated in LDAP search-filter injection?|The directory search filter's expression|The browser's CSS stylesheet|The SQL Server connection pool|The Ethernet frame checksum|LDAP filters have their own operators and escaping rules. SQL escaping is not an interchangeable defense.|Escaping is interpreter- and context-specific.

old:812|H|H11|csrf|What authority is commonly abused by a successful CSRF attack?|The victim browser's automatically attached credentials|The attacker's knowledge of the victim's password|The resolver's DNSSEC signing key|The database's backup encryption key|The browser can send a user's cookies with a request initiated elsewhere. Origin checks, suitable tokens, and cookie policy help constrain this.|An attacker need not read a credential to exploit its automatic use.

old:813|H|H11|session|What is the central failure in session fixation?|A known pre-login identifier stays valid after authentication|An invalid password is accepted because of a DNS error|The browser cannot read an HttpOnly cookie|The server uses a different session ID after logout|The identity transition should rotate and appropriately retire session identifiers. A fixed pre-login token can otherwise become authenticated.|Consider the transition between anonymous and authenticated state.

old:815|H|H11|session|Which property most directly resists session-token guessing?|Unpredictability from secure random generation|A long but sequential account-number prefix|Base64 encoding of the user's email address|A timestamp formatted with punctuation|A long representation is not necessarily high entropy. Predictable input remains predictable when encoded.|Length and unpredictability are different properties.

old:816|H|H12|crest|What protection does Base64 alone provide for a secret value?|None against a reader who can decode it|Confidentiality equivalent to symmetric encryption|Integrity equivalent to a keyed HMAC|Authentication equivalent to a digital signature|Base64 changes representation and is reversible without a secret key. Access controls and actual cryptography address other properties.|An unfamiliar encoding is not secret-key protection.

old:820|H|H13|authz|What useful evidence can source review add to black-box testing?|Internal data flows, checks, and unexposed paths|A guarantee that no runtime bug exists|A guarantee that every deployment matches the source|The exact user's future browser behavior|Source inspection helps find paths and checks that dynamic tests may miss. Configuration, build, and runtime assumptions still need checking.|Code access improves visibility rather than guaranteeing completeness.

old:95|G|G6|php|Why was PHP's historical register_globals behavior risky?|Request values could populate application variable names|It forced every request to use TLS|It prevented SQL strings from being concatenated|It disabled all session cookies|Implicit population could overwrite or influence variables developers treated as trusted. The feature is legacy and removed from modern PHP.|Understand historical trust confusion without assuming a modern feature exists.

old:110|G|G9|crest|What is a sandbox intended to provide for untrusted client code?|A constrained execution environment|A trusted signature on all program inputs|A public copy of the user's private keys|An unrestricted administrator session|A sandbox limits allowed actions or resources. Its effectiveness depends on implementation and configuration, and an escape is a separate vulnerability.|A confinement mechanism is not proof of perfect isolation.

old:167|G|G2|crest|Why must IIS findings identify the exact component handling a request?|Different handlers and modules have different attack surfaces|Every IIS handler runs with identical privileges|All errors originate in the kernel's DNS resolver|An HTTP path uniquely identifies the OS patch level|Server core, modules, application framework, and application code are separate layers. A server-brand label is too coarse to establish a specific flaw.|Locate the vulnerable component rather than blaming a product name.

old:179|G|G1|apache|What does an Apache-style /~alice/ URL commonly suggest?|A user-directory publication feature|A mandatory authenticated administrator endpoint|A file path containing the user's password hash|A TLS certificate issued only to Alice|User-directory mappings can publish selected user content. Confirm configuration and access rather than inferring the whole home directory is exposed.|A URL convention is a configuration lead.

old:181|G|G2|apache|Why should a tester distinguish a commented module-loading directive from an active one?|Only effective configuration determines whether the module loads|Comments are executed before server startup|Every installed module is enabled regardless of configuration|A comment proves the server cannot serve files|Configuration files can contain inactive examples and overrides. Resolve the effective configuration and deployed module set.|Text present in a configuration file need not be active behavior.

old:214|G|G9|crest|What primarily distinguishes a thick client from a thin client?|More application processing is performed locally|It necessarily has higher network privileges|It can operate without any server validation|It cannot communicate over HTTP|Local code and stored data create additional review opportunities. The server must still enforce its own trust boundaries.|Local processing does not confer trusted authority.

old:249|G|G2|crest|An HTTP banner claims Microsoft-IIS/7.0. What is the first evidential limitation?|The disclosed string may be configured or misleading|The string proves every Windows patch is current|The string proves the worker runs as SYSTEM|The string proves every virtual host is identical|A banner helps form hypotheses but is not a signed software inventory. Corroborate important version and platform claims.|Disclosure is a clue, not an attestation.

old:255|G|G2|crest|Which IIS generation is associated with a default Windows Server 2003 installation?|IIS 6.0|IIS 5.0|IIS 7.0|IIS 10.0|This is historical platform knowledge. Modern assessments must confirm actual installed components and support/patch status.|A historical default must carry its version context.

old:299|G|G2|apache|Which option makes the Apache httpd binary print its version?|httpd -v|httpd -k stop|httpd -M|httpd -S|The -v option reports version; -M lists modules and -S reports virtual-host configuration. Distribution binary names can differ.|Command flags answer different inventory questions.

old:513|G|G7|crest|After application-level command execution, what primarily determines the command's OS privileges?|The worker or service execution identity and controls|The application's marketing name|The visitor's browser version|The public HTTP port number|A server product/version alone does not establish SYSTEM, root, or an anonymous account context. Verify identity and isolation.|Do not infer execution privilege from the server brand.

old:518|G|G1|http|A response sets an unfamiliar load-balancer-looking cookie. What can this initially support?|A hypothesis about routing or infrastructure behavior|Proof of a particular exploitable vendor version|Proof that the application has no authentication|Proof that the cookie is a plaintext password|Cookies can reveal routing conventions and persistence. Names and values may be customized, so correlate actual behavior.|Fingerprint artifacts need corroboration.

old:635|G|G5|crest|Which element conventionally marks footer content in HTML5?|<footer>|<blink>|<frameset>|<applet>|HTML5 added semantic elements such as footer. Semantic structure does not itself enforce application access controls.|Markup meaning and security enforcement are separate.

old:90|E|E9|ssh|What does a legacy SSH-1.99 identification string indicate under SSH compatibility rules?|An implementation presenting version-2 compatibility to old peers|An exact operating-system patch level|A guaranteed lack of host-key authentication|A server that uses only plaintext Telnet|The compatibility identification was used by SSH implementations supporting version 2 while accommodating older peers. Test actual enabled algorithms/protocols separately.|Identification strings are protocol clues rather than complete configuration proof.

old:96|E|E1|netcmd|Why does a NetBIOS name-table query not equal a complete Windows browse-list inventory?|It reports registrations on the queried host, not every network member|It always reads the domain's complete computer database|It replaces every LDAP enumeration method|It lists only the tester's browser cookies|Host registration and network/domain inventory are different collection views. Legacy discovery also has coverage limits.|Different enumeration mechanisms expose different scopes.

old:97|E|E4|password|Why could two legacy Windows accounts with the same LM hash have different NT hashes?|LM uppercases input, while NT hashing preserves password case|NT hashes contain a random per-user salt|LM incorporates the user's domain SID|NT hashes are the plaintext password in hexadecimal|Case differences can collapse to the same LM input while producing different NT hashes. Other interpretations require actual evidence.|Equal LM values do not identify exact original capitalization.

old:117|E|E1|ad|What does a legacy __MSBROWSE__ registration concern?|Browser-service discovery of browse domains|A user's interactive browser history|The Kerberos ticket-granting service|An encrypted copy of every account password|This relates to legacy Windows browsing infrastructure. It does not establish modern AD membership or a complete host inventory.|A service's name can be unrelated to web browsing.

old:132|E|E4|netcmd|A Windows authentication attempt returns account-disabled status. What can be inferred about the supplied password?|The status alone does not prove it was correct|It must equal the username|It must be blank|It has been disclosed in the error code|Failure reasons can expose account state without proving a particular credential. Do not infer a password from unrelated disabled/locked status.|Account-state evidence and credential verification differ.

old:158|E|E4|password|How does legacy LM divide its normalized password input?|Two independently processed seven-byte halves|One salted fourteen-byte block|Four independently processed four-byte quarters|Two SHA-256 hashes with per-user salts|LM uppercases and processes up to fourteen bytes as two halves. This makes separate short-half attacks practical.|The construction's structure matters beyond its digest length.

old:168|E|E3|ad|What path conventionally contains ntds.dit on a domain controller?|The Windows NTDS directory|The user's roaming-profile cache|The browser's downloads folder|The SQL Server instance data directory|The default location is under the Windows directory's NTDS folder, but configuration can change it. The database contains directory information.|Know conventional locations without assuming they are universal.

old:200|E|E4|password|Two captured LM values share one seven-byte half's hash. What does that suggest?|The corresponding normalized half is probably the same|The full original passwords are definitely identical|Both accounts necessarily have the same SID|Both accounts necessarily use blank passwords|Independently hashed halves can expose partial equality. NT hashes and additional evidence are needed to assess full-password equality.|Partial hash equality is not full credential equality.

old:279|E|E5|crest|Why does a Meterpreter-specific privilege command not work in an ordinary command shell?|The shell lacks that framework-specific command environment|Every ordinary shell already has SYSTEM privileges|The server must have no local users|The Windows firewall removes every shell built-in|A framework session and raw OS shell provide different interfaces. Local escalation still requires a applicable technique and privileges.|Check the execution interface before blaming the target.

old:283|E|E5|crest|Which prerequisite matters before a tool attempts to read protected Windows credential material?|The process's actual access rights and execution context|Only the remote host's display name|Only the database's listener port|Only whether the shell prints a prompt|Privilege and protections constrain credential access. Loading a framework extension does not automatically grant the underlying rights.|Tool capability does not supply missing privileges.

old:481|E|E2|ad|An account named Helpdesk has a SID ending -500. What does the RID identify?|The built-in Administrator account for that authority|An arbitrary user with an administrator-looking name|The built-in Guest account|The first domain computer account|RID 500 persists when the built-in Administrator is renamed. Check the authority and actual token rather than relying on the name.|Stable identifiers can matter more than display labels.

old:592|E|E9|crest|What is the intended purpose of Windows kernel patch protection on supported x64 systems?|Detect prohibited changes to certain kernel structures|Encrypt every user's NT password hash|Sign every HTTP response automatically|Replace all application privilege checks|Kernel patch protection and protected-process mechanisms are distinct safeguards. Neither is a universal defense against all exploitation.|Separate kernel-integrity controls from process-access controls.

old:5|F|F2|crest|Why must a historical Telnet authentication flaw be checked against an exact affected build?|Similar product or OS names do not prove the vulnerable code is present|Every Telnet server implements the same authentication bug|A default port establishes the installed patch level|A scanner label proves successful exploitation|Legacy vulnerability knowledge is useful only with applicability evidence. Remote-management exposure and a named flaw are separate observations.|Historical recognition should lead to a version-aware discriminator.
